title: Rising as the Lovers Rise: al-Ta'iyya al-Kubra, Part 1
description:
Commentary on the Diwan of Sidi Muhammad ibn al-Habib, Poem 2, al-Ta'iyya al-Kubra, Part 1. A lesson by Shaykh Abd al-Kabir al-Balghithi, recorded 30 October 2026.

The Shaykh opens the longest poem in the Diwan and first explains how Sufi poets arranged their collections: by length, by metre, by rhyme-letter, or by subject. He then takes up the opening verses, "If you wish to rise as the lovers rise, turn aside to Layla with sincere affection," and reads "if you wish" as a call to real spiritual aspiration (himma), illustrated with the parable of the digger.

He describes "rising" as climbing by degrees through Islam, faith (iman) and excellence (ihsan): rising within Islam, rising within faith (down to removing harm from the road), the difference between faith and heedlessness, and vigilance (muraqaba) as keeping company with God. The lesson closes with the hadith of Haritha, a story of al-Junayd and the command to be upright (istiqama), and a closing supplication.

This is an unofficial English translation, edited for readability and read by a synthetic voice. Places where the original audio was unclear are flagged in the written version.
